slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Not covered here? Ask us directly — same working day response.

slots.label: Question 1
slots.default: Why train staff if we already have security tools?

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Because most successful attacks target people, not technology. A convincing phishing email or phone call can bypass technical controls the moment someone believes it’s genuine. Awareness training closes that gap, turning your team into an active first line of defence alongside your tools.

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Sessions cover phishing and malicious attachments, social engineering, password and authentication best practice, secure remote and hybrid working, and how to report suspicious activity. We tailor the content to how your teams actually work and the threats most relevant to them.

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: In plain, practical language with real-world examples rather than technical theory. We start by understanding your working practices, then deliver sessions that help staff recognise suspicious activity and respond confidently.

slots.label: Question 4
slots.default: How often should staff be trained?

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Awareness works best as an ongoing programme rather than a single session. Threats change constantly, so regular refreshers keep security front of mind and introduce employees to the latest techniques as they emerge.

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: Yes. The training is written for everyday employees, not IT specialists. We avoid jargon and focus on the practical decisions people make every day, so everyone leaves knowing what to look out for and what to do.
